title: How does CredentialType work on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of CredentialType and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, CredentialType is issuer-defined binary data identifying what an XRPL Credential attests to. [1]

Its hexadecimal representation is an encoding, not a universal identity category or proof that two issuers apply the same standards. A credential is identified together with its issuer and subject. Permissioned uses must check acceptance and expiration as well as the expected type. Trust in an attestation depends on the named issuer and the receiving application's policy, rather than the familiarity of a label such as KYC. [1]

The public XRPL reference describes CredentialType as part of a larger transaction or ledger lifecycle. Read the associated field definitions and constraints together, rather than treating a single displayed value as complete evidence. The network, account, transaction hash and validated state provide the context needed to interpret the result. Documentation examples explain a format; they are not observations of the current state of a particular wallet. [1]

Author interpretation: preserve the evidence needed to explain CredentialType to another reader and keep pending outcomes visible until they are resolved. Use the same meaning in customer messages and exported receipts. This recommendation follows the documented lifecycle and does not claim a fresh network experiment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
